chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from a man, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who frees his female slave and says to her, 'Your manumission is your dowry,' and then divorces her before consummating the marriage, he said: 'Half of her returns as a slave, and he seeks her consent (to keep her) for the other half.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a man who frees his slave girl with a condition and divorces her before consummation?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the specific mechanics of partial manumission (itq) when coupled with a conditional dowry exchange, a scenario distinct from full emancipation. The ruling that she becomes half-slave and half-free reflects the principle that the 'price' of freedom is not fully settled until consummation or finalization, thereby preserving the master's right to reclaim half her status if the marriage contract is dissolved prematurely. This highlights the nuanced interplay between property rights and marital bonds in Shia fiqh, emphasizing that manumission is not always an immediate, irreversible act but can be contingent upon the completion of specific contractual obligations.
